title: Shortform admin steps as a reusable runtime API
creator: Ariana Patel
description:
Problem: Oncall and support workflows rely on large runbooks or ad-hoc scripts. Engineers repeatedly recreate tiny operational steps (rotate-key, clear-cache, promote-jar, resync-kv) with inconsistent inputs, missing telemetry, and varying safety checks. We need a lightweight, typed, idempotent runtime for "shortform" admin steps that can be launched as first-class tasks from Console, CLI, and API.

Proposal summary: Implement a Shortform Steps service that lets product and SRE teams register tiny, parameterized operational actions (<= 120 lines of code, container or sandboxed function). Each step is stored as a manifest + runnable artifact and exposes: a typed schema, idempotency token, preconditions check, dry-run mode, RBAC enforcement, audit trail, and structured telemetry/events. Steps are executed through a unified API (POST /v1/admin_steps/run) that returns a task id and streaming logs. The runtime supports a sandboxed dry-run environment (no live mutations) and a staged rollout for new steps (canary -> full).

Design notes:
- Manifest format: YAML with fields: id, name, inputs (json-schema ref), outputs (json-schema ref), run_type (container|python-step|shell-safe), precondition-hooks, required-permissions, safety-level (low|medium|high), ttl, retry-policy.
- Execution model: orchestrator schedules step to a short-lived worker pod. Worker validates input schema, runs precondition hooks, acquires ephemeral credential (STS short-lived role) from IAM proxy if required, performs action, streams logs back to client, emits structured events to Telemetry pipeline (step.start/step.complete/step.fail/step.audit).
- Idempotency: steps accept idempotency_key. Replayed requests with same key return prior result or an error when step is non-idempotent by manifest.
- Safety: steps must declare side-effects. High-safety steps require manual approval via Console or explicit OAUTH scope. Dry-run simulates changes and produces diffs where possible.
- RBAC: integrate with existing team RBAC; required-permissions in manifest map to roles in IAM. A separate approval-policy subsystem can require multi-approver gates for certain safety-levels.
- Observability: per-step traces, per-argument cost estimate, token-level latency breakdown. Errors attach to a support ticket template.

Acceptance criteria:
1) API: POST /v1/admin_steps/run accepts manifest id and inputs, returns 202 + task id and streams logs.
2) Dry-run: same manifest can be run in dry-run mode and produces non-mutating result with deterministic diffs for at least 3 example steps.
3) RBAC: a step marked high-safety cannot execute without configured approver flow (manual approve or approval token).
4) Telemetry: every run emits step.start and step.complete events with input schema hash and latency.
5) Sandbox: workers run in restricted environment with no outbound internet by default; ephemeral keys limited by KMS policy.
6) Developer experience: CLI shim (redwood-admin step run ...) and Console button to launch steps with typed UI for inputs.

Deliverables / artifacts:
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood/ops/shortform-steps-prd (draft)
- Runtime prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/shortform-steps (branch: eng/shortform-proto)
- Console mockups: Drive: https://drive.redwood/designs/shortform-steps-v1.png
- Acceptance test harness: unit + e2e dry-run suite under ci/shortform-tests.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: accidental destructive actions. Mitigation: default to dry-run for untrusted authors, require safety-level, add approval gates, and sandboxing.
- Risk: credential leakage from ephemeral keys. Mitigation: integrate with KMS/HSM and short-lived STS tokens; audit every grant.
- Risk: step fragmentation and proliferation. Mitigation: add registry with search, tags, ownership, and deprecation policy.

Next milestones:
- Week 1: finalize manifest schema, basic API, and CLI shim (spike).
- Week 2: build prototype worker + sandbox and dry-run mode.
- Week 3: integrate telemetry and Console UI for launch flow; security review.
- Week 4: dogfood with SRE/Support and iterate on gating and approval UX.
